title: Mechurial Jangjorim Soy-Braised Quail Eggs
shortDescription: Quail eggs are hard-cooked, peeled, and gently braised in soy sauce with garlic until seasoned and glossy.
culturalContext: Mechurial jangjorim is a Korean soy-braised quail-egg side dish. Sweetness, aromatics, chile, broth, and whether meat is included vary. The locked English title spelling is preserved pending language review.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

instructions.heading: Inspect eggs
instructions.action: Use refrigerated clean uncracked quail eggs and discard any cracked or leaking egg.
instructions.safetyNote: Wash hands after handling shell eggs.

instructions.heading: Hard-cook
instructions.action: Cover eggs with water, bring to a gentle boil, and cook until whites and yolks are firm.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: A test egg has a fully firm white and yolk.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not serve soft or runny quail eggs in this draft.

instructions.heading: Cool and peel
instructions.action: Transfer to ice water, cool promptly, then peel with clean hands into a clean bowl.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Shells are removed and eggs remain intact.
instructions.safetyNote: Discard eggs with off odor or contamination during peeling.

instructions.heading: Build the braise
instructions.action: Bring water, soy sauce, rice syrup, garlic, kelp, and optional chile to a simmer; remove kelp after 5 minutes.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The liquid is aromatic and gently bubbling.
instructions.safetyNote: Avoid tasting with utensils used on eggshells.

instructions.heading: Braise eggs
instructions.action: Add peeled eggs and simmer gently, turning, until evenly tan and seasoned.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Eggs are hot and evenly colored.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep the liquid at a controlled simmer to prevent splashing.

instructions.heading: Cool promptly and serve safely
instructions.action: Rest 5 minutes, serve warm, or cool promptly in a shallow container and refrigerate. Halve eggs for diners at choking risk.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Eggs are glossy and the storage container is shallow.
instructions.safetyNote: Whole quail eggs are a choking hazard; cut appropriately and supervise vulnerable diners.

grillSetup: Not applicable; this banchan is prepared on the stovetop or as a seasoned side.
targetInternalTemperature: Cook shell eggs until both whites and yolks are firm; braise peeled eggs until steaming throughout.
visualDonenessCues: Whites and yolks are fully firm
foodSafetyNotes: Cook until whites and yolks are firm.
Cool promptly and refrigerate within 2 hours.
Whole quail eggs can be a choking hazard; cut appropriately for vulnerable diners.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains egg, soy, and wheat/gluten; verify soy sauce labels and prevent cross-contact.

substitutions: Use certified gluten-free tamari only after verifying the label.
Do not substitute pre-peeled eggs without checking the package storage and heating directions.
ingredientSourcing: Choose refrigerated quail eggs in an intact dated carton.
makeAhead: Prepare up to 2 days ahead, cool promptly, cover, and refrigerate.
storage: Refrigerate in braising liquid within 2 hours and use within 4 days pending qualified review.
reheating: Reheat gently until steaming throughout; avoid repeated reheating.
leftovers: Use properly refrigerated leftovers within the approved window and retain choking precautions.
servingSuggestions: Serve in small portions with rice.

faq.question: Why preserve “Mechurial” in the title?
faq.answer: It is a locked inventory field; spelling and romanization require human review.

faq.question: Can the yolks be soft?
faq.answer: No. This draft cooks both whites and yolks firm.
